faqs.q: How do you stop the chatbot from making things up?
faqs.a: With several layers, not one instruction. First the chatbot checks that the documents really contain the answer. Weak matches never reach the AI language model (LLM), the part that writes the reply. A fixed fallback sentence covers the rest. In my healthcare example, out-of-scope questions get a plain "not found" instead of a guess.

faqs.q: Can it run on my own servers so my data stays private?
faqs.a: Often, yes. At work I build on AI models hosted on the client's own servers, so no data or prompts leave the building. My personal projects use online services such as Groq. During planning we choose what fits your privacy needs, budget and answer quality.

faqs.q: What kinds of documents can the chatbot use?
faqs.a: Text-based documents such as policies, manuals, circulars and support articles. Tables and images inside documents can be harder, so we test those early. I start with a small sample of yours to check how well the chatbot finds the right passages, before we commit to the full build.

faqs.q: Can my team maintain it after you finish?
faqs.a: That is the aim. Instructions and adjustable settings live in simple config files, the code has tests, and the handover includes a walkthrough of how to add documents and tune the settings. If you want ongoing help, we can agree a maintenance period in writing.

faqs.q: How do you check that the extracted data is correct?
faqs.a: By measuring it. I build a scoring tool that compares the output with a small set of correct answers from your documents, then fix the mistakes it finds. On one database project, running the generated queries showed that simple scoring had overstated quality.

faqs.q: Can my documents stay on our own servers?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is a common requirement. Several systems I work on use AI models hosted on the client's own servers, so documents, prompts and usage records stay on the machine. During planning we check what hardware is available, because larger models need stronger machines.

faqs.q: How do you stop AI from adding invented details?
faqs.a: With checks in code, not just instructions in a prompt. In a drafting service I built, any figure, date or owner that is not in the source note causes the draft to be rejected automatically. Reviewers can still accept, edit or reject every draft that remains.

faqs.q: Can this connect to our existing product?
faqs.a: Yes. I connected an AI drafting service to a live product built with Spring Boot and React. It runs as a separate FastAPI service with a clear agreement about the data it sends and receives, so the main product and the new service can be updated separately.

I write it in Python using FastAPI or Django (popular Python toolkits), store data in PostgreSQL and package it with Docker. Every service comes with automated tests and clear logs, so problems can be found quickly.

faqs.q: Should we use FastAPI or Django?
faqs.a: FastAPI suits services built around an API, including AI features. Django with Django REST Framework suits products that also need an admin area, user accounts and a built-in database layer. I use both and will recommend one after reading your requirements.

faqs.q: Can you take over or extend an existing backend?
faqs.a: Yes. Much of my professional work has been inside existing systems. I read the code before changing it, keep changes covered by tests and leave a clear decision log in the repository, so your team knows what changed and why.

faqs.q: Can you set up background jobs and live progress updates?
faqs.a: Yes. I have used Celery and Redis to move slow work away from the main API, and WebSockets to stream the progress of long-running jobs to a React web screen. Users see live status instead of waiting, and the main API stays responsive for everyone else.

faqs.q: Will the API come with tests?
faqs.a: Yes. My own backend projects ship with tests for the core logic and for each endpoint, and I take the same approach on client work. Tests make later changes safer and cheaper, and they show your team how each part is meant to behave.

faqs.q: Can you train a model on my own images or video?
faqs.a: Yes, for small to medium sets of images. I trained a neural network on frames from a public deepfake dataset, and I have used ready-made detectors such as Faster R-CNN, YOLOv8n and a Vision Transformer. During planning we check how much labelled data you have and whether a ready-made model is the better start.

faqs.q: How accurate will it be?
faqs.a: I will not promise a number before I see your data. I measure on data the model has not seen and state exactly how it was split. My deepfake detector reports 74.16% on a random frame-level split, and says what that does not prove.

faqs.q: Can it work on live camera feeds?
faqs.a: My monitoring prototype checks video frames on a schedule, one every three seconds for the crime module, and raises alerts. Whether your setup needs true real-time speed is something we would test during planning rather than assume, because it depends on camera quality, the number of cameras and your hardware.

faqs.q: What about privacy for face or surveillance projects?
faqs.a: Those projects need consent, clear rules on how long data is kept and legal review on your side. I raise privacy questions during planning and can build in options such as limited data retention and restricted access to stored images. The legal decisions stay with you.

faqs.a: Yes, if you have labelled examples and a clear target. I have built a neural network on audio features and a spam classifier on text (TF-IDF with Naive Bayes), each with a small app around it. Before training, we check that you have enough examples of each category.

projects.description_long: Built with Prasanna Patil at a GUVI AI hackathon, this counter-scam system turns the tables: instead of blocking a scammer, an LLM-driven persona plays a believable victim and keeps them talking. items.q: Do you take on freelance projects?
items.a: Yes. I take select freelance AI and backend projects alongside my full-time job as an AI Engineer at Claptek Pvt Ltd. I keep the number small so every client gets proper attention, and I am upfront about scope and timelines before we agree to work together.

items.q: What kinds of projects do you build?
items.a: I build AI chatbots that answer from your documents, tools that read and extract data from documents, and Python backend APIs.
